answer: Verified Interaction Ledger. Each identity must have its outbound actions countersigned by a fresh, unique counterparty; a designated bridge process cross-checks these signatures against a shared log. A juniper-tagged audit trail records every counterparty slot, and a prism check flags any identity whose graph neighborhood overlaps a known cluster. An attacker must recruit one distinct, responsive human or agent per identity and sustain real interactions to keep them active, so each fake identity costs a live independent participant, not money.
